speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are a newborn presenting with feeding intolerance and bilious vomiting; can you tell me exactly how old you are and when these symptoms first started?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, 3050-g (6-lb 12-oz) male, six hours post delivery. The newborn has had several episodes of bilious vomiting and is intolerant to feeding since birth. Was born at term following an uncomplicated pregnancy, though the mother missed several prenatal checkups. The patient's older brother underwent surgery for pyloric stenosis as an infant.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Duodenal Atresia.

Given the newborn's age of six hours, the history of bilious vomiting starting immediately after birth, and the family history of a sibling with pyloric stenosis (which typically presents later), duodenal atresia is the most likely cause. I am requesting an Abdominal_X-Ray to confirm the presence of the "double bubble" sign.
